sentences.text: The system architecture is organized around fixed ridge sensors, a staffed operations portal, advisory analytics services, and communications paths that preserve incident command authority.
North Lookout Camera Mast is positioned on the northern rim of the operating area to provide long-range visual coverage of drainages, access roads, and known ignition corridors.
South Lookout Camera Mast covers the opposing viewshed and provides overlapping observation where terrain breaks line of sight from the northern site.
Each camera mast is installed with hardened power distribution, local equipment cabinets, lightning protection, and service access suitable for seasonal maintenance windows.
The camera mast video paths are backhauled through licensed wireless links to the operations network, with cellular service available as a degraded-mode path where coverage permits.
North Lookout Camera Mast sends the Thermal Spot Snippet after local sensor processing identifies a candidate heat signature.
Horizon Ridge Drone Dock is referred to by the site engineering alias Kestrel in drawings and maintenance records for this deployment.
Horizon Ridge Drone Dock is located on a graded pad near the central ridge road so that launch, recovery, charging, and shelter functions remain accessible to maintenance personnel.
The dock includes weather-rated enclosures, charging interfaces, local health monitoring, and a secure network termination for coordination with the rest of the support system.
Horizon Ridge Drone Dock produces the Battery Swap Ticket when its maintenance controller records that a flight battery has reached the configured replacement threshold.
Drone Tasking Service manages approved unmanned flight requests, records mission constraints, and presents task status without acting as an independent authority for flight release.
The Drone Pilot Operator uses Drone Tasking Service to review proposed routes, current dock status, and operational constraints before coordinating any field action through established procedures.
Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine is referred to by the site engineering alias Lantern in architecture diagrams and configuration work orders.
Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine aggregates camera detections, weather inputs, geospatial context, and operator feedback into traceable recommendations for fire detection and suppression support.
Smoke Classifier Module runs as a bounded analytics component that scores visual observations for plume likelihood and passes confidence values to the broader analytics workflow.
The analytics services retain event timing, source identifiers, model version information, and operator acknowledgments so that later review can reconstruct how a recommendation was presented.
MesoWest Weather Fusion Node is referred to by the site engineering alias Brindle in network inventory and integration test records.
MesoWest Weather Fusion Node ingests station observations, forecast grids, and configured quality checks to provide a consistent weather picture for the operating area.
MesoWest Weather Fusion Node sends the Wind Shift Bulletin when its configured weather rules identify a significant change in local wind behavior.
VHF Radio Gateway Repeater provides a monitored bridge between selected radio traffic and operator workstations, with recording and access controls aligned to incident policy.
Caldera Incident Command Portal is the primary operator interface for the Duty Detection Officer, County Emergency Liaison, and other command staff who need consolidated situational information.
The portal displays camera views, detection history, weather context, map layers, and status transitions such as Confirmed Ignition State and Airspace Restricted State.

Talon Air Tanker Dispatch Console supports the Air Attack Supervisor and Tanker Base Manager by presenting aircraft coordination data, loading status, and mission notes relevant to suppression support.

East Retardant Loading Pump and West Retardant Loading Pump are represented in the site layout as monitored ground assets whose readiness and fault indications are visible to authorized operations staff.
Crewline Mobile Tablet provides the Helitack Crew Leader with field access to assigned incident context, map references, and updates that have been approved for mobile distribution.
Across the site, network segmentation, time synchronization, equipment health checks, and audit logging are treated as baseline infrastructure rather than optional add-ons.
